post.caption:
Before standardised containers, cargo was sacks, barrels and crates loaded piece by piece, and that handling was around half the cost of shipping. Malcolm McLean's 1956 insight was not the box itself but that everyone should use the same box, so one crane design works in every port. Loading costs fell by well over 90%, ports were rebuilt around cranes, and shipping got cheap enough that geography stopped driving where things are made.
